actions.reason: Reduce fixed per-call overhead on the encode path. (1) RegexTokenizer.encode_ordinary keys its per-chunk cache on the identity of the steps list returned by ordered_merge_steps, which already returns the same list object only while the merges are unchanged; this replaces a second full dict comparison and dict copy. (2) Uncached chunks are found with set(text_chunks).difference(piece_ids) in C instead of a Python loop over the unique chunks; pieces are encoded independently (separated by a non-token separator), so their order does not affect results. (3) RegexTokenizer.encode skips encode_ordinary for the empty parts produced by re.split around special tokens (they always encode to []). (4) BasicTokenizer.encode builds the result with list(map(ord, s)). Outputs identical; encode_ir ratio 0.9843.

candidate.patch:
diff --git a/minbpe/basic.py b/minbpe/basic.py
--- a/minbpe/basic.py
+++ b/minbpe/basic.py
@@ -253,7 +253,7 @@ class BasicTokenizer(Tokenizer):
                 if len(s) < 2:
                     break
                 s = s.replace(pair, new)
-            return [ord(c) for c in s]
+            return list(map(ord, s))
         ids = list(text_bytes) # list of integers in range 0..255
         merge_map = build_merge_map(self.merges)
         while len(ids) >= 2:
diff --git a/minbpe/regex.py b/minbpe/regex.py
--- a/minbpe/regex.py
+++ b/minbpe/regex.py
@@ -460,13 +460,15 @@ class RegexTokenizer(Tokenizer):
             if steps is not None and (not steps or (steps[0][2] > 255 and steps[-1][2] < 0x10ffff)):
                 sep = chr(steps[-1][2] + 1 if steps else 256)
                 cached = getattr(self, "_encode_ordinary_cache", None)
-                if cached is not None and cached[0] == self.merges:
+                # ordered_merge_steps returns the same list object only while the
+                # merges are unchanged, so the steps identify the cached pieces
+                if cached is not None and cached[0] is steps:
                     piece_ids = cached[1]
                 else:
                     piece_ids = {}
-                    self._encode_ordinary_cache = (dict(self.merges), piece_ids)
-                unique = list(dict.fromkeys(text_chunks))
-                misses = [ch for ch in unique if ch not in piece_ids]
+                    self._encode_ordinary_cache = (steps, piece_ids)
+                # each piece is encoded independently, so their order does not matter
+                misses = list(set(text_chunks).difference(piece_ids))
                 if misses:
                     s = sep.join([ch.encode("utf-8").decode("latin-1") for ch in misses])
                     for pair, new, _ in steps:
@@ -531,7 +533,7 @@ class RegexTokenizer(Tokenizer):
             if part in special:
                 # this is a special token, encode it separately as a special case
                 ids.append(special[part])
-            else:
+            elif part:
                 # this is an ordinary sequence, encode it normally
                 ids.extend(self.encode_ordinary(part))
         return ids

journal.text:
I worked on the encode path in minbpe/regex.py, RegexTokenizer.encode_ordinary. I keyed the per-chunk cache on the identity of the steps list from ordered_merge_steps instead of a full dict comparison and dict copy. I found uncached chunks with set(text_chunks).difference(piece_ids). I made one small change in minbpe/basic.py.

Evaluation 1 was rejected. encode_ir went from 639964071 to 649473184, ratio 1.0149. That first version did not help. Evaluation 3 was rejected at ratio 0.9927 against a required 0.9900. Evaluation 5 was accepted: encode_ir went from 639964065 to 629902892, ratio 0.9843. decode_ir was 1.0015, within limits. Outputs were identical in all three.

I believe fixed per-call overhead in encode_ordinary is a real cost, but the margin is thin. One wrong rearrangement made it slower.

Next I want to wait for the replays. Then I will look at whether the per-chunk loop after the cache lookup still copies data it does not need.
